title: Search in a Binary Search Tree
description:
You are given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST) and an integer `val`.

Find the node in the BST whose value equals `val` and return the subtree rooted at that node. If no such node exists in the BST, return `null`.

All node values in the BST are distinct.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [1, 5000].
root is a valid binary search tree with unique values.
hints: Compare val with the current node's value to decide which single branch to follow.
If val < cur.val, move to cur.left; if val > cur.val, move to cur.right; if equal, return cur.
An iterative loop achieves O(1) auxiliary space instead of O(h) recursion stack space.

examples.explanation: Node 2 is found as the left child of root 4, so return the subtree [2, 1, 3].
Value 5 does not exist in the BST, so return null.
Node 15 is the right child of 10 and has right child 20, so return [15, null, 20].
